headline: Colossal Biosciences reportedly in talks to raise new capital at $20B–$30B valuation
summary: The de-extinction startup, known for projects like the woolly mammoth, is seeking new funding that could significantly boost its valuation from $10.2 billion to up to $30 billion.
details: Colossal Biosciences is reportedly in talks to raise new funding at a valuation between $20 billion and $30 billion, according to Axios. This comes roughly 16 months after its previous $10.2 billion valuation.

The five-year-old startup, known for its de-extinction projects like the dire wolf, has started generating revenue over the last year. Details on the lead investor or the exact capital sought are not yet clear.
Colossal co-founder and CEO Ben Lamm previously outlined three main revenue streams. These include offering conservation technology to governments, as seen with the UAE's $60 million investment.
The company has also spun out three successful startups: Breaking (plastics breakdown), Form Bio (computational biology, $30M funding), and Astromech (AI predictive modeling, valued at $2B).

Future plans include spinning off its artificial animal womb technology, which could be ready next year for human fertility applications. If successful in reintroducing extinct animals, Colossal may also generate revenue from biodiversity credits.
This fundraising effort aligns with a broader boom in deep-tech sectors, including longevity tech and alternative energy.

headline: Trump's latest AI czar resigns after just three months, continuing rapid turnover
summary: Chris Fall, director of the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), has resigned after only three months, following a pattern of rapid departures from the role.
details: Chris Fall, director of the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), has resigned after just three months. This marks another rapid departure from a key AI leadership role within the administration. No specific reason was given for his exit.

Fall's predecessor, Collin Burns, also left in less than a week in April, reportedly "pushed out" due to his prior work with Anthropic amid a dispute between the company and the Trump administration. Before Burns, venture capitalist David Sacks stepped down in March from a similar role.

CAISI, operating under the National Institute of Standards and Technology, is tasked with developing technical standards and testing methods for AI models, including assessing cybersecurity risks. Its mission is crucial for AI governance.

Despite its mandate, CAISI was notably absent from the White House's new "Gold Eagle" AI safety oversight program announced earlier this month. This program aims to create a clearinghouse for cybersecurity vulnerability coordination.

The resignation also follows recent controversies, including the Commerce Department's temporary ban on Anthropic's Mythos and Fable models. Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis has since called for an independent, industry-run standards body, mirroring CAISI's mission.

Furthermore, the administration is reportedly considering efforts to ban Chinese open AI models, sparking debate. CAISI has released reports on some Chinese models but has not been transparent about its testing processes, raising questions about its effectiveness.
